title: Server stalls for 5-10 s at a time while a large move writes to the Pi's SD card
description: During the 7.9 GB move of the map data to Internal storage on the Pi (SD card), /api/health once took 5 s and /api/jobs gave no answer within 10 s; with nothing running every probe answered in 10-90 ms. The copy and hash are async streams, so the likely cause is SQLite's synchronous writes (WAL fsync on the main thread) waiting on an SD card saturated by the copy's writeback. Not confirmed. To check: measure event-loop delay during a large move; consider throttling transfer writes, fsync of the copy in steps, or fewer progress writes while a transfer runs.
notes: Root cause confirmed 18 Nov 2026 on the Pi: during a large write to the SD card (ext4, data=ordered, default vm.dirty_ratio=20% of 8 GB, about 1.6 GB may sit unwritten), Node's main thread blocks in pwrite64 from SQLite (state D, wchan do_get_write_access: waiting on the jbd2 journal, which must first flush the big file's ordered data). 2.4 GB written with dd while making a DB write each second: worst DB write 5.6 s (1.1 GB dirty). With vm.dirty_bytes=64 MB / background 16 MB: worst 1.4 s. With the writer calling fdatasync every 16 MB (default kernel settings): worst 0.33 s, health never over 43 ms, same total time (58 s vs 53 s; the default's 31 s was data still in memory). Fix: in Outpost's own large writers (collection move copy in collections/transfer.ts, the HTTP download fetcher, map region extract, P.533 maps, imagery), fdatasync the target every 16 MB; optionally also set vm.dirty_bytes in deploy/pi/install.sh.
close_reason: Fixed: large writes fdatasync every 16 MB (core/synced-write.ts). Real move of 857 MB onto the Pi's SD card: worst health 0.09 s (was 5-10 s).

title: Map: estimated radio range from any point (a hilltop, a planned site), using the repeaters' range code
description:
Owner, 18 Nov 2026. Use case: choose a place on the map (often a hill, where someone would set up a radio) and see how far a radio there could reach, drawn as the same estimated-range outline a repeater gets.

How: reuse what the repeaters use. GET /api/maps/sight-range (at, aerial, station) already works out, bearing by bearing, how far a station stays in sight of an aerial over the installed terrain; the repeaters' map draws that as an outline. Offer it for any point: from a long press or a found place ('Estimated radio range from here'), from the line-of-sight tool's point A, and from a saved place.

Inputs, with sensible defaults and said plainly: the height of the aerial above the ground at the point (default: held in the hand, about 1.5 m; or on a mast), and the height of the other station's aerial (default: another handheld, 1.5 m; or a car, or a base station on a mast). Where the point is a summit, say so in the result.

Wording: this is not a circle and not a promise. Call it 'Estimated range' as the repeaters do, and say what it is in one line: the ground a radio at this point can see over the terrain, for the heights given; radio often reaches less (power, the band, woods and buildings) and sometimes more (reflections). Show it as the terrain-shaped outline (it is not round: a hill blocks one side), with the furthest and nearest distances. No terrain installed: say heights need terrain, as the height readout does, rather than drawing a plain circle that looks like an answer.

Not: power or band in the estimate (line of sight only, as for repeaters), until propagation is joined to it. Works anywhere in the world where terrain is installed.
notes: Owner, 18 Nov 2026: start it from the map's own menu for a point: a long press on a phone or tablet, a right-click with a mouse (the same menu that offers Save a place, Measure, Draw and the Sun times), as an item such as 'Estimated radio range from here'. Also from a found place, a saved place and the line-of-sight tool's point A, as in the description.

title: NAS (SMB) share on the Pi lost one 4 KiB block in a 2.3 GB download; not reproduced
description: 18 Nov 2026: a Geofabrik extract written through the cifs mount (//192.168.1.100/docs, vers=3.0, kernel 6.6.73-v8-16k, default cache=strict) had 4096 zero bytes at offset 1877356544 (the last quarter of a 16 KiB page), on the NAS disk itself (read with O_DIRECT). No reconnects in /proc/fs/cifs/Stats. Three 2.3 GB files written afterwards the same way (append-only, slices of at most 16 KiB, 2 MB/s) read back identical, and about 12 GB of ZIM downloads to the same share passed their SHA-256. So rare, cause unknown (kernel cifs client on 16K pages, or the NAS). Downloads with a published checksum now catch it and Retry fetches again; downloads with no published checksum (Natural Earth, map regions, documents) cannot. Options if it recurs: read back what was written and compare with a checksum taken as the bytes arrived; mount with cache=none; a newer kernel.
close_reason: Cause not found, but every download is now read back against what was written and repaired; see docs/storage.md

title: Catalogue check: fall back to a first-byte request when HEAD answers 404
description: nvlpubs.nist.gov and the Met Office file service (cold cache) answer HEAD with 404 while serving the file. Fix and remove the NOT TESTED notes.

title: Maps: write waypoints-as-places in batches off the busy path
description: importTrack inserts each marker and its search entry one by one on the server's own thread (~0.2 ms each), which is why one file may turn at most 5,000 waypoints into saved places (MAX_WAYPOINTS_AS_MARKERS in modules/maps/annotations.ts). Batch the inserts and the search upserts, or do them as a job, then raise the cap towards the reader's 20,000.

title: Radio sheets: re-verify yearly and fill the gaps
description: CHU, BBC long wave, repeater tones, HF emergency nets and marine channel numbers beyond 16, 70 and 9 could not be verified from primary sources on 2026-11-15 and are left out or marked.
notes: 2026-11-16 (branch feat/more-sources): marine VHF channels 13, 6, 8, 72 and 77 added to the emergency frequencies sheet by number and use, quoted from MCA MGN 324 (M+F) Amendment 2 (no frequencies given there, so none added). CHU: nrc.canada.ca refused again (403). BBC long wave: not confirmed; the Met Office Shipping Forecast factsheet (Jan 2025) predates the reported closure. Repeater tones: ukrepeater.net robots.txt disallows its data folders, nothing fetched. HF emergency nets: no primary source looked for. Still open.
